title: Period 'double transposition' = one table, keyed column order plus keyed row order (whole text, unequal columns)
raw_text: "Under the title of double transposition, the said works allude to cases where the columns are inscribed in the table in an order determined by a key, and where the letters in each column are inscribed not from top to bottom ... but in an order likewise determined by a key, the same or different. (Sometimes the name 'double transposition' is used for another system which should be called 'retransposition.')" (Givierge 1925, English translation). Hitt 1916, Case 2-c: "both lines and columns are rearranged by means of a key word or key words ... This cipher is not infrequently met with because it seems to offer safety by use of two key words".
source_locator: Givierge, Cours de cryptographie (1925), English translation, ch. on tabular transpositions, p. ~94, https://archive.org/details/french-colonel-marcel-givierges-1925-book-cours-de-cryptographie-cryptography-course ; Hitt, Manual for the Solution of Military Ciphers (1916), Case 2-c, https://www.gutenberg.org/files/48871/48871-0.txt
original_read: full text of translation / Gutenberg text, read by procedure agent; not re-read by main thread
people_institution: Givierge (French army cipher section); Hitt (US Army)
connection_to_messages: None documented. Givierge is a French handbook available to a Swiss reader in 1937; no source ties it to Viktor or Werner Oswald, Patvag, or the BLUME correspondent. Its relevance is that a 1925 reader looking up 'double transposition' would meet this one-table system, not two successive columnar passes, which is what experiments 01-27 assume.
contradictions: Hitt says Spanish cipher text uses a 24-letter alphabet without K; T1 has 2 K. Hitt and Givierge both describe the system as breakable by anagramming, so it is a weak system. Nothing makes it likelier than double columnar; it is a separately sourced, untested family.
confidence: procedure attested as period usage of the name; use by these senders unattested
computational_consequence: New family for H4. Cipher = columns read in column-key order, each column's letters in one shared row order. For a complete rectangle (615 = 15x41 = 41x15 = 5x123 = 3x205; 160 = 8x20, 10x16, 16x10, 20x8, 5x32, 32x5) cutting the ciphertext into w chunks of h letters and reading the chunks across row by row gives exactly experiment 18's 'Nihilist rectangle read by rows' problem (sets of w, one column key, sets in any order). Experiment 18 ran on the raw text, not on this rearrangement. Experiment 20 covered n x n squares only and lists 'the whole-text rectangle read by columns with unequal columns' as not covered.
derivation_preparation: Column key: keyword ranked alphabetically, ties left to right (Givierge MARSEILLE example, reproduced in analysis/28). Row key: separate keyword of length h or numeric permutation; Givierge allows the same key only when lengths match (i.e., squares, already covered by 20). No filler: last row incomplete (Givierge).
bounded_variants: T1: complete-rectangle widths w in {15, 41} first (h 41, 15), then incomplete widths w 8-30 where the long columns are the first (615 mod w) plaintext columns. T2: w in {8, 10, 16, 20}. Preamble/tail trims only as in 17 (0-20 letters), not new.
prior_search_overlap: 18 (same reduced problem, raw text only); 19 (lag profile, power against this family unmeasured); 20 (squares only). Not covered by any double columnar experiment.
proposed_test: Step 1, no target: plant 20 T1-length texts in this family at w 15 and 41 and measure whether experiment 19's lag statistic and 14's contact statistic already reject them; if they do, the family is already excluded at those widths and the test stops. Step 2, only if step 1 shows no power: rearrange and run 18's unchanged solver with fresh seeded-apart controls (pass rule >= 8/10 per band, thresholds fixed before target), then T1 at w 15, 41 and T2 at w 8, 10, 16, 20. Incomplete widths need a long-column assignment search and a separate frozen design.
negative_result_means: A negative at the complete-rectangle widths excludes only those widths under 18's model and budget. It says nothing about incomplete rectangles, other preparation, or double columnar.

title: Real 1937 Spanish telegrams as plaintext calibration for the scoring model and acceptance threshold
raw_text: See calibration-telegrams.md: P1 (Valencia to Buenos Aires, 5 Jun 1937, plain language, 1,654 letters incl. service lines); M1-M8 (Republican ministerial telegrams, Feb-May 1937, deciphered, printed 1994, 3,668 letters); H1-H4 (Hitt 1916, out of period, 607 letters).
source_locator: Pochat, Olivar 9(11), 2008, pp. 145-149 (P1); Gordillo Coucieres, Historia y Vida, Apr 1994, via https://www.ugr.es/~aquiran/cripto/museo/marcantabrico.htm (M1-M8); Hitt 1916 (H1-H4)
original_read: transcriptions only; no original telegram image seen
connection_to_messages: None. Calibration material only. Not evidence about the BLUME plaintext.
contradictions: Not commercial; M1-M8 are one source in modern orthography (accents, N-tilde) and need normalization; only two independent 1937 sources.
confidence: real period telegraphese, thin and non-commercial
computational_consequence: Measures the gap audit 23 flagged: every negative so far uses modified-novel plaintext. Tests whether real telegraphese clears the -5.10 acceptance threshold and whether recovery rates hold on it.
derivation_preparation: Normalize: strip accents, N-tilde -> N, letters A-Z only; drop service lines from P1 as a separate variant. Do not add PUNTO or STOP.
bounded_variants: Two variants for P1 (with/without service lines). Plants at T2 length (160) from single messages; T1-length (615) plants only from P1 and M1, which are long enough without concatenation.
prior_search_overlap: None; all prior controls use literary proxy text (01-solver/plaintext.py).
proposed_test: Freeze plan; (a) score each normalized untransposed text with the solver's quadgram model and report against -5.10; (b) rerun 26's supplied-K2 isolated stage on plants built from P1 and M1 (no target).
negative_result_means: If real telegrams score below -5.10, earlier negative target results lose force under that threshold. If they pass, no key or system is validated.

title: Keyword numbering: repeated letters numbered left to right
raw_text: Key MARSEILLE numbered 7 1 8 9 2 4 5 6 3; plaintext LA SIXIEME DIVISION PARTIRA CE SOIR; cryptogram AIRIX SREPS IIAEO CMNEL DAOSV TRIII; table left incomplete, no filler.
source_locator: Givierge 1925, pp. 94-95 (archive.org, as HE-P01); Hitt 1916 Case 2-a (MEXICO = 4 2 6 3 1 5)
original_read: translation text; reproduced by script in analysis/28-historical-evidence
computational_consequence: No new test. 24-27 already generate left ties; right ties are a modern test choice that could be dropped to halve a future phrase list.
derivation_preparation: stable sort of key letters, ties by position
bounded_variants: left ties only (documented); right ties undocumented

title: Preparation leads: Spanish 24-letter cipher alphabet, terminal X, Nationalist code ban
raw_text: Hitt 1916: "a cipher whose text is Spanish will be prepared with the following alphabet: A B C D E F G H I J L M N O P Q R S T U V X Y Z"; Spanish examples end FINISX, NOCHE X. FRUS 1936 vol. II doc. 719 (Bowers, 12 Sep 1936): Burgos told the military at Vigo "no messages in code shall be permitted".
original_read: Hitt text yes; FRUS via fetch summary, not facsimile
connection_to_messages: None to the Oswalds. The FRUS item concerns the Nationalist end of the route four months earlier; it may explain why the telegrams were presented as five-letter code-like groups (T2 stamped Cde). It is a report of an order to one port, not the order.
contradictions: T1 has 2 K, against Hitt's no-K rule. Terminal X fits T1's X-rich end only post hoc.
computational_consequence: None for the target now. Could define one plaintext-preparation variant for controls (no K/W, terminal X) if a frozen calibration is run.

title: New contextual names from the Victor M. Oswald legation file (not keys)
raw_text: OSWALD (Moritz Victor) ne le 15 Novembre 1909; VICTOR M. OSWALD; Miraconcha 13 3o, San Sebastian; 'Osswald in Burgos, Banco Guipuzoano, San Sebastian' (sic, Hunziker letter, 19 Apr 1937)
source_locator: BAR E2001E#1000/1571#787* (B.31.51), Unterlagen_0000002 (French expulsion decree copy, 28 Oct 1937) and Dokument_0000003 (letter 15 Feb 1939); BAR E4320B#1974/47#277 subdossier 66 (Hunziker letter, per oswald-trail agent)
source_tier: PRIMARY (machine OCR; images of Dokument_0000003 not viewed by main thread)
connection_to_messages: Names of the sender and his addresses. No source says any of them was a key. The Miraconcha address dates from 1938-39; in January 1937 Viktor was in Burgos.
contradictions: OSWALD has W; T1/T2 contain no W, which is irrelevant to keys (key letters need not occur in the message) but matters for any crib use.
computational_consequence: None recommended. Would add a handful of phrases to a list already searched in 24-27; the solver's negative results give no reason to expect them, and no evidence selects them.
bounded_variants: MORITZ VICTOR OSWALD, MORITZ VIKTOR OSWALD, BANCO GUIPUZCOANO (only if a future frozen phrase test is justified on other grounds)
prior_search_overlap: OSWALD, VICTOR, VIKTOR, VICTOR OSWALD, SAN SEBASTIAN, BURGOS already in 24/phrases.py

title: Other Oswald telegrams: one 1937 telegram referred to without text; one 1938 plain-language telegram
raw_text: (a) Hunziker letter, 19 Apr 1937: a telegram from Zurich said Viktor could not come to Paris (text not in dossier). (b) Telegram, Hendaye 1938, to Bundeshaus Bern: "sehr geehrter herr doktor muss dringenst ins ausland reisen und ersuche sie ueber legation paris durchreiseerlaubnis zu erreichen entschuldigen sie neue muehewaltung besten dank und gruesse victor oswald" ("dear doctor, must travel abroad most urgently and ask you to obtain transit permission through the legation in Paris; excuse the renewed trouble; many thanks and regards, Victor Oswald").
source_locator: (a) BAR E4320B#1974/47#277, subdossier 66 (oswald-trail agent, image read); (b) BAR E2001E#1000/1571#787*, Unterlagen_0000004, OCR lines 588-630
people_institution: Viktor Oswald; Hunziker; Swiss Division of Foreign Affairs
connection_to_messages: Same sender. Neither is cipher traffic. (b) shows Viktor writing his own plain telegrams in German telegraphese, which bears on preparation style only.
contradictions: BLUME telegrams have W = 0 in 775 letters, so they are not German plaintext under transposition; (b) does not change that.
computational_consequence: No additional ciphertext. No key relationship can be tested.

title: BLUME candidate: 'Blume Otto' in a Condor Legion decorations list
source_locator: Hidalgo Salazar, La ayuda alemana a Espana 1936-1939 (1975), p. 223, Google Books snippet
original_read: no (search snippet; adjacency of Salamanca and the name unverified)
connection_to_messages: None. Name match only; no address, no Oswald link. Context: the French consul reported Viktor in constant contact with German agents in San Sebastian (Swiss Legation Paris, 6 Jul 1939), so a German recipient is not implausible, but that is not evidence for this man.
contradictions: A two-word address BLUME SALAMANCA fits a registered telegraphic address better than a surname without a street.
proposed_test: Read p. 223 in a library copy; check telegraphic-address registers for BLUME.
